packageRules.description: CoreDNS is pinned as a build arg rather than a base image, so point Renovate at the GitHub release tags. A bump here rebuilds the plugin against a new CoreDNS; the plugin tests are what catch an API change.
Go module updates for the plugin itself. These are all CoreDNS's own dependencies, so let them batch.

Renovate leaves indirect Go dependencies alone by default, which is wrong here: this module imports almost nothing directly, so every dependency that ends up in the shipped binary is indirect. The image build merges this go.mod into CoreDNS's, and the higher version wins, so an indirect bump here is the only way to patch a CoreDNS dependency ahead of a CoreDNS release.

CoreDNS v1.14.x builds against caddy v1, and a Go major bump changes the import path rather than just the requirement, so a v2 PR fails the build and cannot be merged until upstream CoreDNS moves. Follow CoreDNS's choice instead of Renovate's.
Never open a PR that unpins an image tag.
